title: Slim wakeup default loads: defer Skills + lug index
description: Currently wakeup Step 3 loads WAI-Skills.jsonl (32 skill entries, ~15k tokens) + Step 4 lists active lugs (20 files, not read but listed). Move both to lazy-load: load on-demand when user asks 'show active work' or skill lookup happens.
acceptance: Wakeup Step 3: Skip WAI-Skills.jsonl load. Add note: 'Use /wai-status or /wai to see active work'
Wakeup Step 4: Don't list lugs. Defer to /wai-status command or explicit user request
Briefing shows 'Active work: [count] items (lazy-loaded, ask /wai-status for details)'
All lug details loaded only if user asks or closing out
impact: Reduce default wakeup from ~46k to ~30k tokens. Cuts context overhead by 35%.
blockers: Signal about context estimation accuracy must ship first
scope_verified_by: user feedback (Session 73: local optimization work for Wheelwright Framework)
routing_notes: Work item for Wheelwright Framework's session 73. Stays local during execution. Becomes a signal if optimization proves broadly applicable.
acceptance_criteria: Wakeup Step 3 no longer loads WAI-Skills.jsonl by default
Wakeup Step 4 no longer lists individual lugs — shows count only
Briefing shows 'Active work: [count] items' with lazy-load note
Full lug/skill details accessible via /wai-status on demand
